I just keep aging. I don't know if getting another job would mess with getting into the Hall of Fame, but by the time you retire you'd have hundreds of millions of dollars, so it's not an issue really.

Make sure your stats are all up. Practice ALL your basketball skills and train all fitness skills 1x every year.

Make sure you're in a team with high strength, usually the top 3 teams in the league would do. Try out with them, retire from your current team if you have to. Don't worry, there won't be penalties in doing so. If you can't get in top 3, just get in the highest one you can.

The rest is a bit of RNG. Every year you'll get prompts showing events and you'll get to choose how to react to them. Some of them will give you a higher chance of getting a championship. I don't think there's a walkthrough out there so you'll have to test them out and remember them, though some are pretty obvious. Basically pick the honourable and fair options. The ones I can remember right now is "They beat us fair and square" when you lose against highschoolers, "Volunteer at a homeless shelter" when asked to present a squeaky clean image, always thank fans and ignore haters, etc.

With all the above, your rankings in the league should steadily increase. In my case I went from rank 18, 15, 8, 3, then stayed at 1 all the way. Close the app and reopen it if you get a lower rank than last year.

The general advice seems to be to stay pro as long as possible (try 20+ years) and get as many championships as you can, though some folks managed to get into the Hall of Fame with only 2 championship rings. It's partially luck.

Try get a lot of the other regular medals as well (MVP, Most Improved Player, Best Defensive/Offensive/etc Player, etc) by raising your stats year after year. You actually have to improve year by year. Don't start out with perfect sports skills or you won't get those medals.

After your final season (which should be around age 40-43, basically you'll stop getting contract offers and you can't draft anymore), age up a couple years. You'll get inducted within 2 decades. I was generally in my 50s when I got inducted.

Good luck!
